Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 11 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 294 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Draft:

I think students would benefit from being able to attend classes from home, as long as it is offered as an option and not forced on everyone.

The first reason is flexibility. Some students are sick for long periods, live far from school, or have family duties that make a regular schedule hard to keep. A girl recovering from surgery, for example, could keep up with her math class from her bed instead of falling weeks behind. A student who lives an hour away from the nearest school could save that travel time and spend it on homework or sleep. Both of them get a real education they might otherwise miss.

The second reason is comfort and focus. Some students struggle in crowded classrooms. Noise, bullying, and social pressure can make it hard to concentrate. At home, a student can work in a quiet space, pause a recorded lesson to take better notes, and ask the teacher questions in a chat instead of in front of thirty classmates. Shy students often speak up more online than they ever would in person.

Of course, distance learning has real problems. Students can get distracted by phones and games, and not every family has a reliable computer or internet connection. Learning at home can also be lonely, since school is where many people make friends and learn to work in groups. Because of this, schools should not make it mandatory, and they should help families that lack the right equipment.

Still, the benefits outweigh the costs when students get to choose. Distance learning gives sick, distant, or anxious students a way to keep learning, and it lets others decide what setting works best for them. Schools should offer it as one more path to a good education.
